common_name: Ping Tung Eggplant (Long Slender Heat-Tolerant Taiwanese Eggplant)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost; transplant after all frost danger passes and soil is warm. Ping Tung, from Taiwan, is an early, heat-tolerant, highly productive long eggplant well suited to Gulf South summer conditions.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once nights stay reliably warm. Ping Tung produces long, slender, glossy purple-lavender fruit up to 18 inches, with thin, tender skin and mild, sweet, nearly seedless flesh that holds its shape well in stir-fries and grilling. Originating in Taiwan, it is notably early to bear and remains productive through the hottest, most humid stretch of a Gulf South summer, when many Western eggplant varieties slow down or decline. Harvest fruit while still glossy for the best texture, since overripe fruit dulls and develops tougher flesh and larger seeds, and pick every few days to keep the vigorous plants producing steadily.
